limitation_26_pin_change_notifications.diagnosis_confirmed: The entry's own proposed fix was right. UEdGraphPin::MakeLinkTo moves two pointers and stops; UEdGraphSchema_K2::TryCreateConnection, which is what the graph editor runs, also calls PinConnectionListChanged on both ends.
limitation_26_pin_change_notifications.change: The builder now calls UEdGraphNode::PinConnectionListChanged on both ends of every connection it makes, and PinDefaultValueChanged after every pin default it writes.
what_that_unlocks: UK2Node_DynamicCast::NotifyPinConnectionListChanged (K2Node_DynamicCast.cpp:347) promotes the Cast node's Object pin out of PC_Wildcard, so a Cast compiles instead of failing with 'The type of Object is undetermined.'

UK2Node_CallFunction::PinDefaultValueChanged -> FDynamicOutputHelper::ConformOutputType (K2Node_CallFunction.cpp:1239) retypes a meta=(DeterminesOutputType) output from its class pin. GameplayStatics.CreateSaveGameObject carries that meta (GameplayStatics.h:976) and now hands back the requested subclass rather than a bare USaveGame*.
limitation_26_pin_change_notifications.safety: Each call is guarded by !Pin->IsPendingKill(), because a notification can destroy a pin (bIsBeadFunction suicide, orphan-pin removal). Connections resolve their pins by name each iteration rather than caching pointers, so a node that reconstructs mid-build does not invalidate a later link.
limitation_26_pin_change_notifications.why_the_public_entry_point: PinConnectionListChanged on UEdGraphNode is what the schema calls. UK2Node's override resets a connected input pin's autogenerated default before forwarding to NotifyPinConnectionListChanged; calling the inner one directly would skip the literal clearing the editor does.

platform_changes.as_result_pin_role: A dynamic cast names its result pin "As" plus the target type's DISPLAY name (K2Node_DynamicCast.cpp:63), which for a Blueprint generated class is neither the asset name nor anything a caller can compute from its own spec. The connection resolver takes the role AsResult and asks the node through GetCastResultPin(). Three connections in the F4 graph use it.
platform_changes.target_scoped_variables: FBPNodeFactory::CreateVariableGet / CreateVariableSet took a scope key and refused anything but 'self' (BPNodeFactory.cpp, 'scope %s not supported in v1'). They now take scope 'target' with targetClass, call FMemberReference::SetExternalMember, and the node grows a self input pin (UK2Node_Variable::CreatePinForSelf, K2Node_Variable.cpp:112) for the object to act on. The class is loaded and the property looked up before the node is created, so a misspelled variable name is a factory refusal rather than a missing pin two steps later. This is one of the three fixes limitation 25 listed; it does not close 25, because a created UUserWidget's children still have no member on its generated class to name.

save_load_mechanism.typed_cast: Two routes, each proven where it is needed. On save, GameplayStatics.CreateSaveGameObject's SaveGameClass pin default is /Game/MCPGenerated/BP_StaminaSave.BP_StaminaSave_C, and PinDefaultValueChanged conforms its DeterminesOutputType output to that subclass. On load, GameplayStatics.LoadGameFromSlot returns a bare USaveGame* and a Cast node types its Object pin from the connection, through PinConnectionListChanged. The cast result is addressed by the pin role AsResult.
save_load_mechanism.target_scoped_variable_access: VariableSet {var_name: SavedStamina, scope: target, target_class: /Game/MCPGenerated/BP_StaminaSave.BP_StaminaSave_C} with its self pin wired from the cast result and its value pin from CurrentStamina; VariableGet with the same routing on the load side. SetFloatPropertyByName was the fallback and was not needed, and would not have covered the read half: KismetSystemLibrary has setters by name, not getters.
save_load_mechanism.slot: SaveSlotName variable, default "MCPStamina", wired into DoesSaveGameExist, SaveGameToSlot and LoadGameFromSlot rather than repeated as a literal.
save_load_mechanism.ordering: Load at t=1, save at t=5, each once behind a bDidLoad / bDidSave guard. Load before save is what makes the round trip provable: a later session reads what the earlier one wrote before it overwrites the slot with its own value.

walls: A graph spec is the whole graph, and variables are additive. clear_existing_graph defaults true and there is no node identity to merge against, so extending a generated Blueprint means resending every node; meanwhile a variable the spec stops mentioning stays on the asset forever. BP_StaminaCharacter now carries the previous session's variable set alongside this one's. Limitation 32, and the next chunk's primitive.

200 nodes is a real ceiling once a quarter of the graph is string composition: every logged value costs one Conv_*ToString and about two Concat_StrStr, because there is no string-literal node. The F4 graph sat at exactly 200 for two builds and a value had to be traded away to add one. Limitation 33.

Moving a Character by writing its capsule's RelativeLocation with set_property reports success, reads back the new value, and leaves the character able to fall through the floor: its own graph reported z=29.4 then -801, -2626, -5430 at terminal velocity. The same class spawned fresh with spawn_actor at the same place reported z=110.149994 on every tick. Delete and respawn; do not write the transform. Limitation 34.

A named child widget of a created UUserWidget is still unreachable (limitation 25). Target-scoped variable access, added here, was one of the three fixes that entry listed and it is not enough on its own.

Nothing in the catalog can press a key (limitation 31). InputKey LeftShift, K and L build and bind; the PIE proof drives the same variables from the Tick timeline. Unchanged, and still not claimed as fired.

notes: Two limitations closed by four lines of notification. The Cast node, DeterminesOutputType, and everything else that depends on a pin-change callback were broken by the same omission: the builder wired pins with MakeLinkTo and never told the nodes. That is the whole of limitation 26, and it had been read correctly when it was filed.
Limitation 23 was one line of our own code standing where the engine's rule already was. Removing it made three designs available at once, and the cost was a predicate naming five node types.

The save value is read back at the far end rather than echoed: MCP_LOAD prints the float that came out of the loaded object's own SavedStamina, and session two's stamina variable is at its 100.0 default one line earlier, so the restored number cannot have come from anywhere but the file.

The house style held again: no runtime property read and no screenshot during PIE, so every claim is a number the graph printed about itself. maxWalkSpeed comes from GetMaxSpeed, speed from GetVelocity, hudPercent from GetRenderOpacity, and the restored stamina from the save object.
recommended_next_goal: Limitation 32, in two halves: node identity so a generated graph can be patched instead of resent, and a declared-set variable pass so a Blueprint stops accumulating dead members. Then limitation 33's real fix, a FormatText node with typed argument pins, which the pin-change notifications landed here have probably already made possible.
